versions.short: The bill would require states to give the Department of Justice whatever information it asks for when investigating or prosecuting suspected fraud in certain federally funded programs, including Medicaid, SNAP food assistance, TANF cash aid for needy families, certain coronavirus-related payments and grants to states, and any other program the Department identifies as vulnerable to fraud. Federal agencies could use that information only for fraud-related law enforcement and could not share it for unrelated administrative or commercial purposes. The Department of Justice would also have to report to Congress each year on how many information requests it made to state agencies, which programs they covered, and how many fraud investigations and convictions the information helped produce.
